items.title: fix: preserve OpenAI encrypted reasoning item ids through the anthropic surface
items.body:
## Summary

Fixes #5186. OpenAI validates encrypted reasoning payloads against the reasoning item id they were issued with. The Anthropic surface drops that id on egress (the `redacted_thinking` block only carries `type` and `data`) and mints a random one on replay, so every replayed redacted block fails with `Encrypted content item_id did not match the target item id` and traffic silently degrades to fallbacks. This PR carries the `(item_id, encrypted_content)` pair through the round trip in a Bifrost-private envelope inside `data`, decoded only at the final destination-provider conversion.

## Changes

- New codec in `providers/utils/reasoningenvelope.go`: base64 JSON envelope `{_bifrost, v, provider, item_id, payload}`. Strict unwrap: exact magic, version, provider allowlist, non-empty id and payload, encoded-size cap, control-character check on the id. Anything that does not parse is raw legacy data and behaves exactly as before. Wrap is idempotent and falls back to the raw payload if the encoded envelope would exceed the cap.
- Egress to an Anthropic-format client: when the actual source provider is OpenAI (from `ExtraFields.Provider`, not the requested model, since routing and fallbacks can change it) and the item has both an id and encrypted content, the redacted block's `data` holds the envelope. Anthropic-origin `data` stays byte-identical. Items with both a summary and encrypted content now emit the thinking blocks and the redacted block instead of dropping the encrypted state.
- Replay: a recognized envelope restores the original `ResponsesMessage` id and stays wrapped in the neutral `EncryptedContent`. Deferred decoding keeps provenance intact for fallbacks.
- Final mile: `ToOpenAIResponsesRequest` unwraps only when the destination provider is exactly OpenAI. Any other destination through the shared converter (Azure, OpenRouter, fallback-swapped requests) drops the hidden item rather than forwarding foreign ciphertext.
- Known gap, unchanged: the streaming state machine allocates one block per output item, so a streamed item carrying both a summary and encrypted content still mixes deltas onto one block. Pre-existing behavior; a proper fix needs a per-item sibling block and is out of scope here.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [x] Core (Go)
- [ ] Transports (HTTP)
- [x] Providers/Integrations
- [ ] Plugins
- [ ] UI (React)
- [ ] Docs

## How to test

```sh
cd core
go test ./providers/anthropic/ -run 'Redacted|Envelope' -v
go test ./providers/utils/ -run Envelope -v
go test ./providers/openai/ -run Envelope -v
```

Live validation: built `bifrost-http` from this branch, captured a `redacted_thinking` block from a GPT-5.x reasoning model through `/anthropic/v1/messages` (the `data` field now carries the envelope), then replayed it verbatim in a tool loop. On v1.6.3 that replay fails with the item-id 400 every time; on this branch it succeeds. Anthropic-origin thinking replay through the same build is unchanged.

items.title: fix(semanticcache): don't cache or replay raw payloads stripped from the client
items.body:
## Summary

With `store_raw_request_response` on and `send_back_raw_request` / `send_back_raw_response` off, core keeps the raw provider payloads for logging and drops them from the response it hands to the client. That strip happens in `tryRequest` after the post-hook chain returns.

Since #7304 the semantic cache serializes the response inside `PostLLMHook`, which is before that strip. So the cache entry ends up with `raw_request` / `raw_response` in `extra_fields`, and the next hit replays them as part of the short-circuit response. A client that should never see the upstream payloads gets them, and it can be a different caller from the one whose request produced them.

## Changes

Raw payloads describe the upstream call made for the request that wrote the entry. A hit makes no upstream call, so they never belong in a replay. The hitting request's own send-back policy is also not known when the hit is served: core derives the drop flags per attempt in the request worker (`applyRawCaptureSignals`), after the pre-hooks have run, so a hit served from `PreLLMHook` always sees them unset.

- `PostLLMHook`: remove `raw_request` / `raw_response` from the serialized bytes before they go to the writer. This covers both the single-response write and the per-chunk stream accumulator, since both use the same bytes. The live response isn't touched, so core's strip and the logging plugins behave as before.
- Cache hits (non-stream and stream): clear both fields on the replayed response, so entries written before this change don't leak them either.
- A request that asks for raw payloads back still gets them on a miss. On a hit it gets none, since no upstream call was made for it.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [ ] Core (Go)
- [ ] Transports (HTTP)
- [ ] Providers/Integrations
- [x] Plugins
- [ ] UI (React)
- [ ] Docs

## How to test

```sh
cd plugins/semanticcache
go test -race -count=1 ./...
```

`plugin_raw_fields_test.go` has five tests. Against current `dev`, four fail (raw fields in the stored entry, in cached stream chunks, and on both replay paths) and one passes (live response untouched). With the fix all five pass. The two ownership tests from #7233 used `raw_response` as their marker for a mutation made after the hook returns; they now mutate the response content instead, and still fail if the writer serializes after the hook returns. The whole module passes under `-race`.

items.title: [Bug]: Claude Code OAuth passthrough strips signed thinking blocks with empty text
items.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I have searched existing issues and discussions to avoid duplicates
- [x] I am using the latest version (or have tested against main/nightly)

### Description

**Area:** core/providers/anthropic — raw request body path (`StripEmptyThinkingBlocks`), Claude Code `/anthropic` OAuth passthrough

## Summary

On the Claude Code passthrough route (`/anthropic/v1/messages`, UA `claude-cli/*`, `Authorization: Bearer sk-ant-oat…`, raw request body forwarded), Bifrost removes every assistant `thinking` content block whose `thinking` text is empty — even when the block carries a valid, non-empty `signature`. Claude Code in OAuth mode requests `redact-thinking-2026-02-12` (in `anthropic-beta`); under that beta the Anthropic API itself returns thinking blocks with `"thinking": ""` plus a signature, and Claude Code replays them verbatim on every later request of the session. The API accepts them back. Bifrost's raw path is therefore not verbatim for exactly the shape the API produces, which (a) makes the request bytes diverge from direct Claude Code traffic, invalidating the prompt cache from that block onward whenever the same conversation crosses paths, and (b) removes the signed reasoning block that Anthropic's documentation says must be preserved on the assistant turn preceding a `tool_result`.

## Observed behavior

1. Anthropic emits the empty-text signed block. Stream captured from a Claude Code session talking to `api.anthropic.com` directly (no Bifrost), `anthropic-beta` containing `redact-thinking-2026-02-12`, `thinking: {"type":"adaptive"}`:

```
data: {"type":"content_block_start","index":0,"content_block":{"type":"thinking","thinking":"","signature":""}}
data: {"type":"content_block_delta","index":0,"delta":{"type":"thinking_delta","thinking":"","estimated_tokens":null}}
data: {"type":"content_block_delta","index":0,"delta":{"type":"signature_delta","signature":"CAISswIKpgEIERgCKkCEMMUY…"}}
…
"usage":{…,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":16}}
```

2. Claude Code replays it. The next requests of that session contain, in the assistant turn:

```
{"type": "thinking", "thinking": "", "signature": "CAISswIKpgEIERgCKkCEMMUY…"},
{"type": "text", "text": "…"},
{"type": "tool_use", "name": "Bash", …}
```

followed by the user `tool_result`. Sent directly to `api.anthropic.com` this request returns HTTP 200 (three such requests in one short session, all 200).

3. Through Bifrost the block is gone. Same request replayed through `/anthropic/v1/messages?beta=true` with the OAuth passthrough active (provider `anthropic`, `x-bf-vk` virtual key): the body that leaves Bifrost is byte-identical to the client's EXCEPT that `messages[6].content[0]` (the thinking block above) is removed — `content-length` 162136 → 161703 in the interactive session; `messages[6].content` becomes `[text, tool_use]`. Every other request of the session (six of seven, none of which carried a thinking block) was byte-identical.

4. Cache impact, measured with the same request body sent 1 s apart: direct → `cache_creation_input_tokens: 55737`; through Bifrost → `cache_read_input_tokens: 46831`, `cache_creation_input_tokens: 8890`. Everything from the stripped block to the end of the conversation is re-cached.

5. The API still answered HTTP 200 without the block, so there is no hard failure today — but continuity of the signed reasoning is lost, and Anthropic's tool-use-with-thinking rule (the final assistant message before a `tool_result` must start with its thinking block) is only not enforced for this shape at the moment.

## Root cause

`core/providers/anthropic/utils.go` `StripEmptyThinkingBlocks` removes a `thinking` block when `thinking == ""` OR `signature == ""`. It runs unconditionally on the raw-body path (`core/providers/anthropic/requestbuilder.go` lines 418 and 691), i.e. also for the Claude Code passthrough. The accompanying test (`utils_test.go`, case "strips block with empty thinking even if signature is non-empty") documents the assumption "Anthropic rejects them with 'each thinking block must contain thinking', even if the signature is valid" — that assumption does not hold for `redact-thinking-2026-02-12` traffic, where empty-text signed blocks are the API's own output.

## Suggested fix

Keep blocks whose `signature` is non-empty; strip only when the signature is empty (the cross-provider replay case the function was written for: OpenAI/Gemini never emit signatures). If the older "each thinking block must contain thinking" rejection must still be handled for non-redacted traffic, gate the empty-text strip on the absence of a `redact-thinking-` beta in the request (or skip the strip entirely when `IsClaudeCodeMaxMode(ctx)` / the raw passthrough is active — the client already sends what the API gave it). Update the test case accordingly.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Bifrost with provider `anthropic` (any key), governance VK, `client.enforce_auth_on_inference: true`.
2. Claude Code 2.1.267 logged in with a claude.ai (OAuth) account: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080/anthropic ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS="x-bf-vk: <vk>" claude`. Ask for something that triggers a tool call after the model thinks (e.g. "create hello.txt", then "put \"hello\" to hello.txt", then "What did you change?").
3. Capture the request Bifrost sends upstream (e.g. a logging reverse proxy as the provider `base_url`) and compare with the request Claude Code sent (a logging proxy in front of Bifrost): the assistant turn's `{"type":"thinking","thinking":"","signature":"…"}` block is missing upstream; everything else is byte-identical.

### Expected behavior

On the Claude Code OAuth passthrough the request body should reach Anthropic unmodified apart from the fields Bifrost owns (`model`, `stream`). A thinking block with an empty `thinking` text but a non-empty `signature` is a valid block that the Anthropic API itself produced under `redact-thinking` and accepts back; it must not be stripped.

### Actual behavior

signed thinking blocks are stripped with empty text

### Affected area(s)

Core (Go)

### Version

v2.1.1

### Environment

```text
Bifrost release v2.1.1 (transport 2.1.1 / core 1.8.6, linux/amd64 binary; source tag `transports/v2.1.1`, commit c193745) · Claude Code 2.1.267 (Anthropic SDK 0.112.1)
```

### Relevant logs/output

```shell

```

### Regression?

_No response_

### Severity

Medium (some functionality impaired)

items.title: [Bug]: web_search version auto-upgrade (20250305 → 20260209) now hard-fails with 400 for HIPAA-configured Anthropic orgs (code_execution not available)
items.body:
## Summary

Since 2026-11-02 ~20:00 UTC, every Anthropic `/v1/messages` request that passes through Bifrost with a `web_search_20250305` tool declared is rejected by Anthropic with HTTP 400 when the upstream API key belongs to a HIPAA-configured organization:

```json
{"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"The requested features are not available for HIPAA-configured organizations: code_execution."}}
```

The client never declares `code_execution`. Bifrost normalizes the client's `web_search_20250305` tool to a bare `web_search` and re-serializes it as `web_search_20260209` for Opus 4.7+ / Sonnet 5+ models (`core/providers/anthropic/responses.go`, `ResponsesToolTypeWebSearch`, unless `server_tools.web_search` is pinned in the model's governance parameters). The `20260209` version enables dynamic filtering, which Anthropic implements as server-side code execution. Anthropic's HIPAA/BAA terms exclude code execution ("dynamic filtering for web search ... is not eligible for ZDR or HIPAA"), so the request fails before the model runs.

This is the same rewrite reported in #9150. The difference is the impact: #9150 described a downstream thinking-replay failure on later turns; this is a deterministic 400 on the very first request, i.e. a full outage of web-search-enabled traffic for HIPAA-configured orgs. Anthropic appears to have started enforcing the restriction around 2026-11-02 20:00 UTC; the same request bodies, with `code_execution` blocks in the response, were accepted earlier the same day.

## Evidence

- Same API key, same request body sent directly to `api.anthropic.com` (keeps `web_search_20250305`): 200, no `code_execution` blocks, hundreds of successful calls in the same window.
- Same key via Bifrost `/anthropic/v1/messages`: 400 with the error above, every request, across several Bifrost virtual keys and provider keys that map to HIPAA-configured orgs.
- Fleet-wide after the cutoff: zero `code_execution` blocks in any Anthropic response via Bifrost, consistent with Anthropic now rejecting them for these orgs rather than silently running them.

## Request

1. Preserve the client's explicit versioned server-tool type (`web_search_20250305`) instead of upgrading it to the latest version for the model. Upgrading changes the request's compliance surface, not just its capability.
2. At minimum, document that the auto-upgrade to `web_search_20260209` implies `code_execution`, and that HIPAA/ZDR orgs must pin `server_tools.web_search=web_search_20250305` in governance model parameters.

## Environment

- Bifrost transports v2.2.6 (also reproduced the rewrite on v2.3.2 source).
- Provider: `anthropic`, models `claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`.
- Request path: `/anthropic/v1/messages`, streaming.

items.title: [Bug]: Gemini provider replaces a client-supplied `extra_content.google.thought_signature` with `skip_thought_signature_validator`, and writes the sentinel on every replayed function call (old turns, all models)
items.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I have searched existing issues and discussions to avoid duplicates
- [x] I am using the latest version (or have tested against main/nightly)

### Description

When a request with tool-call history is converted for the native `gemini` provider, every replayed `functionCall` part for which Bifrost cannot recover a signature from its *own* encodings gets `thoughtSignature: "skip_thought_signature_validator"`:

```go
// core/providers/gemini/utils.go L2428-2430 at a404aa7e (convertBifrostMessagesToGemini); same fallback in responses.go L4962-4964
if part.ThoughtSignature == nil {
    part.ThoughtSignature = []byte(skipThoughtSignatureValidator)
}
```

The only sources it recovers a real signature from are the `<call_id>_ts_<base64url>` id suffix and `reasoning_details[].signature`. `ChatAssistantMessageToolCall.ExtraContent` — added in #4470 precisely so that `extra_content.google.thought_signature` survives the typed structs, and documented in the schema as "forwarded verbatim through any proxy/gateway layer without loss" — is never read by the Gemini request converters (no reference to `ExtraContent` anywhere under `core/providers/gemini/`). #2226, which introduced the sentinel, describes it as applying "only when a replayed Gemini function call has no reusable thought signature"; in the P1 case below a reusable one is present and still gets replaced.

Seven hand-written requests, local build, Gemini upstream replaced by a local recorder (no live traffic). Identical results on `080a6bb` (2026-10-01) and on `main` `a404aa7e` (2026-10-07; version files transports 2.2.6 / core 1.11.3):

| # | inbound | what the client sent | what reached the Gemini upstream |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | `/v1/chat/completions` | `tool_calls[].extra_content.google.thought_signature = <real base64>` (the field Google's own OpenAI-compatible endpoint uses for this) | **signature discarded, sentinel written instead** |
| P2 | `/v1/chat/completions` | `id = "call_1_ts_<base64url>"` (Bifrost's own encoding) | real signature preserved |
| P3 | `/v1/chat/completions` | no signature (history from a non-Gemini model) | sentinel (the documented last-resort case) |
| P4 | `/v1/chat/completions` | no signature, call in an **old** turn (a later plain user message follows) | sentinel — although the API only validates signatures of the current turn |
| P5 | `/anthropic/v1/messages` | `tool_use` + `tool_result`, no signature | sentinel; the model `Content` is also emitted without `role` (will file separately) |
| P6 | `/genai/v1beta/...:generateContent` | real `thoughtSignature` on the functionCall | preserved (but `role: "model"` dropped, `id` = function name added) |
| P7 | `/genai/v1beta/...:generateContent` | functionCall without signature | sentinel |

On a larger local replay (357 Anthropic-format requests with tool-call histories, 240 of them containing function calls), the sentinel was written on 362/362 replayed function calls with model id `gemini-2.5-flash`; of 1,470 OpenAI-format requests produced by six client libraries that reached the upstream, 992 contained function calls — 1,497 calls, sentinel on all 1,497.

Why I think this is worth a look rather than just the documented fallback:

1. Google's thought-signature page says `skip_thought_signature_validator` "should be a last resort as it will negatively impact model performance". P1 means a client that does the right thing — keeps `extra_content.google.thought_signature` as Google's OpenAI-compat endpoint emits it — gets the last resort anyway, silently.
2. P3/P4/P7 apply the last resort by default, for all history (not just the current turn, which is what the API validates) and for all model ids (the requirement is documented for the Gemini 3 family; for comparison, LiteLLM's converter only writes the dummy when the model is `gemini-3*`), without a log line or a switch.
3. Because the token is written by the gateway, the application cannot tell that its history is replayed with validation disabled; the only visible symptom is lower answer quality on multi-step tool use.

### Steps to reproduce

Bifrost config: `gemini` provider with any key, `base_url` pointed at a local HTTP recorder (or a real key and the request log). Then:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'authorization: Bearer x' -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
 "model":"gemini/gemini-2.5-flash","max_tokens":50,
 "tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"get_weather","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"city":{"type":"string"}}}}}],
 "messages":[
  {"role":"user","content":"weather in Paris?"},
  {"role":"assistant","content":null,"tool_calls":[{"id":"call_1","type":"function",
     "function":{"name":"get_weather","arguments":"{\"city\":\"Paris\"}"},
     "extra_content":{"google":{"thought_signature":"AQJyZWFsLXNpZ25hdHVyZS1ieXRlcwM="}}}]},
  {"role":"tool","tool_call_id":"call_1","content":"sunny"}]}'
```

Observed upstream body (`contents[1]`):

```json
{"parts":[{"thoughtSignature":"skip_thought_signature_validator",
           "functionCall":{"id":"call_1","args":{"city":"Paris"},"name":"get_weather"}}],"role":"model"}
```

P2–P7 are the same request shape with the variations listed in the table.

### Expected behavior

`"thoughtSignature":"AQJyZWFsLXNpZ25hdHVyZS1ieXRlcwM="` for P1; the sentinel only where no reusable signature exists and the API would otherwise reject the request.

### Actual behavior

P1: real signature replaced by `skip_thought_signature_validator`; P3/P4/P5/P7: sentinel written on every replayed call regardless of turn position or model.

### Affected area(s)

Core (Go)

### Version

main a404aa7e (transports 2.2.6 / core 1.11.3); also 080a6bb

### Additional context

Sketch of what I would try (untested):

```go
// convertBifrostMessagesToGemini (utils.go, before the fallback) and the same spot in responses.go
// 1. honour the OpenAI-compatible field before falling back
if part.ThoughtSignature == nil && len(toolCall.ExtraContent) > 0 {
    var ec struct{ Google struct{ ThoughtSignature string `json:"thought_signature"` } `json:"google"` }
    if json.Unmarshal(toolCall.ExtraContent, &ec) == nil && ec.Google.ThoughtSignature != "" {
        if d, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(ec.Google.ThoughtSignature); err == nil { part.ThoughtSignature = d }
    }
}
// 2. scope the last resort: calls in the current turn, models that validate, and a warn-level log (or a provider option)
if part.ThoughtSignature == nil && inCurrentTurn && modelValidatesSignatures {
    part.ThoughtSignature = []byte(skipThoughtSignatureValidator)
}
```

Emitting `extra_content.google.thought_signature` on the response side as well (next to the `_ts_` id suffix) would let clients that follow Google's convention round-trip it unchanged. Happy to re-run the seven cases against a branch.

items.title: [Bug]: DeepSeek shim forces thinking off for tool-call turns with no replayed reasoning — silently, and upstream accepts it
items.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I have searched existing issues and discussions to avoid duplicates
- [x] I am using the latest version (or have tested against main/nightly)

### Description

On an OpenAI-compatible DeepSeek request, when the caller asks for thinking (`thinking: {"type": "enabled"}`)
and the message history contains an assistant **tool-call** turn that carries no `reasoning_content`, Bifrost rewrites the outbound body to
`thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` — leaving `reasoning_effort` set. The caller gets no signal at all: the captured
responses carry only `extra_fields.routing_info` and `x-bifrost-*` routing headers, so the requested thinking mode
disappears with nothing to detect.

Code: `requiresDeepSeekThinkingDisabled` / `applyDeepSeekThinkingCompatibility` in `core/providers/deepseek/deepseek.go`:

```go
// 2. A history containing an assistant tool_call turn that carries no replayable
//    reasoning. DeepSeek requires reasoning_content to be replayed on tool_call turns and
//    400s without it; when the caller cannot supply it, thinking has to stay off.
```

Two problems with that branch, most important first:

1. **The premise does not hold against DeepSeek's live API.** A direct call to
   `https://api.deepseek.com/chat/completions` with `thinking: {"type": "enabled"}`, `model: "deepseek-flash"`,
   tools declared, and an assistant tool-call turn **without** `reasoning_content` returns **HTTP 200** and streams
   reasoning (58 chars, `[DONE]` received). No rejection to avoid. The same request through Bifrost returns no
   reasoning at all.
2. **The state the branch reacts to is ordinary, not exceptional.** A thinking-enabled request does not guarantee a
   reasoning block; upstream itself returns `reasoning_tokens: 0` for realistic agentic bodies (measured below, no
   Bifrost in the path). A turn produced that way has nothing to replay, and every later request whose history still
   holds that tool-call turn is forced to `thinking: disabled` — the caller's requested mode is lost for the rest of
   the conversation, silently.

The other branch of the same function (forced `tool_choice`) **is** reproducible: `tool_choice: "required"` with
thinking on returns HTTP 400 `Thinking mode does not support this tool_choice`, so that half looks justified.


### Steps to reproduce

Gateway-only, no client SDK needed. DeepSeek provider with default OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

**1. Inbound request to Bifrost** — thinking requested, tools declared, one assistant tool-call turn with no
`reasoning_content`:

```bash
curl -sS http://<bifrost>/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $BIFROST_VIRTUAL_KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "deepseek-flash",
    "max_tokens": 800,
    "stream": true,
    "stream_options": { "include_usage": true },
    "thinking": { "type": "enabled" },
    "reasoning_effort": "high",
    "tools": [{ "type": "function", "function": { "name": "read", "description": "Read a file",
      "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": { "path": { "type": "string" } }, "required": ["path"] } } }],
    "messages": [
      { "role": "user", "content": "Read a.md and tell me the number inside." },
      { "role": "assistant", "content": "",
        "tool_calls": [{ "id": "call_1", "type": "function", "function": { "name": "read", "arguments": "{\"path\":\"a.md\"}" } }] },
      { "role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_1", "content": "# a.md\nthe answer is 42" },
      { "role": "user", "content": "State the number." }
    ]
  }'
```

Observed: HTTP 200, no reasoning at all (`reasoning_tokens` absent), and with any logging proxy between Bifrost and
upstream the outbound body is:

```json
{ "model": "deepseek-flash", "max_completion_tokens": 800, "stream": true, "stream_options": {"include_usage": true},
  "messages": [ ...same history... ], "tools": [ ... ],
  "reasoning_effort": "high",
  "thinking": { "type": "disabled" } }
```

(`reasoning_effort` kept while `thinking` is flipped — the two fields disagree.)

**2. Same request, only the assistant turn changed** (2 trials each, same logging proxy):

| inbound `reasoning_content` on the tool-call turn | outbound `thinking` | upstream reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| field absent | **`{"type":"disabled"}`** | 0 chunks |
| `""` (empty string) | `{"type":"enabled"}` | 41 chunks / 39 tokens |
| `"I will read the file first."` | `{"type":"enabled"}` | 34 chunks / 32 tokens |
| no tool-call history at all | `{"type":"enabled"}` | 99 chunks / 98 tokens |

**3. Control, straight to DeepSeek** (bypassing Bifrost), same model, streaming, thinking enabled:

| upstream request | result |
|---|---|
| tool-call turn without `reasoning_content` | **HTTP 200**, reasoning 58 chars |
| tool-call turn with `reasoning_content: ""` | HTTP 200, reasoning 220 chars |
| `tool_choice: "required"` | **HTTP 400** `Thinking mode does not support this tool_choice` |
| `reasoning_effort: "max"` | HTTP 200, reasoning 81 chars |
| no `thinking` field | HTTP 200, reasoning 0 chars |

**4. Why a tool-call turn can legitimately carry no reasoning** — same provider, same thinking parameters, no
Bifrost in the path, `stream: true`, `thinking: {"type":"enabled"}` + `reasoning_effort: "high"`:

- Minimal bodies think every time: `"hello"` 179/101 chars, `"Say pong."` 205/145, `"@HANDOFF_EXAM_AUDIT.md Resume
  work and continue directly."` 776/617, `"Resume work from the handoff document and continue directly."` 923/1956,
  `"Which is bigger, 9.9 or 9.11? Think carefully."` 675/662, `"List two prime numbers under 10."` 142/159.
- The exact body Bifrost forwarded upstream for a real agentic turn (system prompt, 33 tool declarations, an
  instruction to resume work from a handoff file, `max_completion_tokens: 256000`) returns **HTTP 200 with 0
  reasoning characters and `reasoning_tokens: 0`**, reproduced 4 times.
- In that body, cutting both the tool list and `max_completion_tokens` restored reasoning (39 chars / 9 tokens and
  48 chars / 11 tokens), so the outcome depends on the request shape as a whole rather than on a single field.


### Expected behavior

An outbound request keeps the caller's requested thinking mode whenever upstream accepts the request, and any compatibility rewrite is visible to the caller.

### Actual behavior

`thinking: {"type":"enabled"}` becomes `{"type":"disabled"}` for every request whose history holds a tool-call turn without `reasoning_content`, even though DeepSeek accepts that request unchanged. The turn stays in the history, so the rewrite repeats on each later request and thinking stays off for the rest of the conversation. Nothing in the response tells the caller this happened.

### Affected area(s)

Core (Go)

### Version

v2.1.1

### Environment

```text
- OS: Linux 7.2.2-arch1-1 (x86_64), Docker 29.7.2
- Image: maximhq/bifrost@sha256:12d6bbab32b44e3bb88869c6f5ca9304b53a9c43cb55c57a29f851037bcc19e1 (running container bifrost-app-1)
- Provider: deepseek (dedicated provider implementation), single key, no use_anthropic_endpoints (default OpenAI-compatible mode);
  upstream path observed: POST /chat/completions with `authorization: Bearer`
- Client: dsh (deepseek-official route, chat-completions protocol) — sends thinking enabled + reasoning_effort "max";
  the same behavior reproduces with plain curl, so the client is not part of the trigger
```

### Relevant logs/output

```shell
Outbound body captured between Bifrost and `api.deepseek.com` (same request, two turns of one conversation):


turn 1  inbound:  thinking={"type":"enabled"} reasoning_effort="max" max_tokens=256000
        outbound: thinking={"type":"enabled"} reasoning_effort="high" max_completion_tokens=256000
        upstream: reasoning_content streamed, completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens > 0

turn 2  inbound:  thinking={"type":"enabled"} reasoning_effort="max" max_tokens=256000   (history now holds turn 1's tool call)
        outbound: thinking={"type":"disabled"} reasoning_effort="high" max_completion_tokens=256000
        upstream: no reasoning_content, completion_tokens_details: {}


Rule fit over 38 captured requests: 33/33 conversation requests satisfy "tools present ∧ a `tool` result in history ∧
no assistant `reasoning_content` ⇒ outbound `thinking: disabled`"; the 5 exceptions are tool-less title requests whose
caller had already sent `disabled` itself.

Caller-visible response headers for a request the shim fired on — no signal of the rewrite:


x-bifrost-original-model, x-bifrost-provider, x-bifrost-request-type, x-bifrost-resolved-model,
x-bifrost-routing-info-*, x-bifrost-trace-id, x-bifrost-upstream-latency-ms
extra_fields: { request_type, routing_info }   # no thinking/reasoning note
```
### Relationship to #5887

This is the same guard with a narrower trigger — the surviving half of the change that closed #5887, not a new
regression from it.

- Before `dd927388` ("deepseek thinking fixes (#5888)", which closes #5887), `disableThinkingForForcedToolChoice`
  carried the broader rule: "(e.g. synthetic/injected history, or a turn produced while thinking was off) — DeepSeek
  requires prior reasoning_content to be replayed once thinking is on, **so if any assistant turn is missing it,
  thinking must stay off for the whole request**". Any assistant turn without reasoning disabled thinking — which is
  exactly the #5887 report (its multi-turn repro used a plain assistant turn with no reasoning).
- #5888 narrowed the gate to assistant **tool-call** turns (plus forced `tool_choice`) and stated the reasoning:
  "DeepSeek's reasoning replay requirement is scoped exclusively to assistant tool-call turns — plain assistant turns
  without tool calls do not require `reasoning_content` to be replayed".
- Confirmed on v2.1.1: plain multi-turn conversations keep `thinking: enabled` (captured), tool-call histories
  without replayed reasoning get `disabled` (captured). So the #5887 half is fixed, and this report covers the half
  the fix intentionally kept.

The ask is the same scrutiny for the remaining branch: the control in step 3 could not reproduce the rejection it
exists to prevent, and the state it reacts to (a tool-call turn with no reasoning) is produced by ordinary agentic
traffic, because a thinking-enabled upstream request can come back with `reasoning_tokens: 0`.

### Regression?

Not determined (no earlier version tested in this environment). The narrower behavior documented under issue #5887 (plain multi-turn conversations without tool calls keep thinking on) is present in v2.1.1 — this report is the remaining tool-call case.

### Severity

Medium (some functionality impaired)

items.title: [Enhancement]: SQLite log store loses all historical token/cost statistics when retention deletes raw logs
items.body:
## Problem

On the SQLite log store (the default, zero-dependency deployment), `log_retention_days` deletes raw rows and **all historical token/cost statistics disappear with them**. There is no aggregation layer that survives retention:

- The hourly pre-aggregation (`mv_logs_hourly` + the archive work in #7349–#7354) is **Postgres-only** — every path starts with `if db.Dialector.Name() != "postgres" { return }`, and the implementation relies on materialized views, plpgsql functions, `set_config`, and advisory locks, none of which exist in SQLite.
- On SQLite, every dashboard/stats query scans the raw `logs` table directly, so statistics and retention are welded together: keeping the numbers means keeping multi-GB payload blobs; pruning the payloads means losing the numbers.

SQLite is the default backend promoted for single-binary/docker deployments — the population least likely to run Postgres or an external TSDB, and least able to self-serve around this gap. Today their only options are "grow without bound" or "lose all history".

## Production evidence

Single-node k8s deployment, v2.2.1, SQLite backend. **This is a single-user gateway** — one operator running coding-agent workloads through it, no multi-tenancy, no team/customer scoping, roughly 2,300 requests/day. There is no "small deployment" escape hatch here: at *one* user the backend is already in this state.

- 17 days of logs → `logs.db` = **17.7 GB** for only **26.5K rows** (~700 KB/row; chat-wire histories replay full prior content including reasoning, so `input_history` dominates: ~8 GB total payload for well under 1 GB of distinct conversation).
- Stats-style aggregation over a 7-day window: **200 s** per query — not from missing indexes (there are 30+, including a purpose-built covering index `idx_logs_histogram_cover`), but because `ANALYZE` is never run on the SQLite store (verified: no `ANALYZE` call anywhere in the codebase; `sqlite_stat1` absent), so the planner under-estimates the fat-row table and picks row-id lookups over the covering index. One manual `ANALYZE` (19 s) took the same query to **0.4 s–15 s**.
- With retention at 30 days the file still plateaus around 30–35 GB, and every row deleted permanently erases that day's token/cost totals — for a single user who just wants to know what they spent last quarter, there is no supported way to get that number.

The volume driver is not user count but agent-shaped traffic: long multi-turn sessions where every request replays the full prior history. A single agent user generates this load; nothing about the SQLite path anticipates it.

## Expected behavior

Token/cost statistics should survive raw-log retention on the SQLite backend too, the way #7349–#7354 makes them survive on Postgres (finalize/seal hourly aggregates before deleting raw rows; serve archived analytics with coverage metadata). Separately, query planning on SQLite needs `sqlite_stat1` maintained (`ANALYZE` after migrations, `PRAGMA optimize` on close) — without it even recent-window stats queries are pathologically slow on fat-row databases.

## References

- #7349 #7350 #7351 #7352 #7354 (Postgres hourly archive chain)
- `framework/logstore/matviews.go`, `framework/logstore/cleaner.go`, `framework/logstore/sqlite.go`

items.title: [Bug]: Bifrost sends reasoning_content instead of reasoning to OpenAI compatible upstream providers
items.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I have searched existing issues and discussions to avoid duplicates
- [x] I am using the latest version (or have tested against main/nightly)

### Description

When using Bifrost to route traffic to an OpenAI compatible provider like vLLM or the OpenAI provider itself, multi turn reasoning preservation currently fails on subsequent turns.

This happens because Bifrost forwards the previous chain of thought using the `reasoning_content` property inside the assistant's past messages. However, vLLM recently aligned with the OpenAI API specification and now requires this field to be named `reasoning`.

Because Bifrost sends `reasoning_content`, vLLM silently ignores the past reasoning trace. As a result, the model loses its chain of thought context from previous turns degrading multi turn performance for reasoning models.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure Bifrost to route to a vLLM backend using the OpenAI or vLLM provider configuration.
2. Complete a first turn with a reasoning model, and capture the assistant's response (which includes reasoning).
3. Send a subsequent (Turn 2) chat completion request, passing the previous assistant message back to Bifrost:

```
"messages": [
  {
    "role": "user",
    "content": "First prompt"
  },
  {
    "role": "assistant",
    "content": "Final response",
    "reasoning_content": "Deep Thoughts here..." 
  },
  {
    "role": "user",
    "content": "Follow up question"
  }
]
```

4. Observe the upstream payload Bifrost sends to vLLM. It forwards `reasoning_content`.
5. Because vLLM expects `reasoning`, the preservation fails and the model acts as if it has no memory of its previous chain of thought.

### Expected behavior

When routing requests to vLLM or other strict OpenAI compatible providers, Bifrost should map the reasoning traces in past assistant messages to the reasoning key.

### Actual behavior

Bifrost passes the payload upstream using the reasoning_content key. Because vLLM strictly expects reasoning based on the current OpenAI spec, the provider silently drops or ignores the chain of thought context. The model then generates its next response as if it has no memory of the previous turn's reasoning process

### Affected area(s)

Core (Go)

### Version

v1.6.11

### Environment

